header:
Money Myth:
Big Money to Invest?

lines.text: 4 in 10 Americans own zero stock. Yet $1 buys a slice.
lines.say: Four in ten Americans own zero stock. Yet one dollar buys a slice.

lines.text: Gallup's 2026 count: 42% of US adults owned no stock at all.
lines.say: That's Gallup's twenty twenty-six count: forty-two percent of US adults owned no stock at all.

lines.text: Ownership rose from 52% in 2016 to 62% in 2025, then dipped to 58% in 2026.
lines.say: Ownership rose from fifty-two percent in twenty sixteen to sixty-two percent in twenty twenty-five, then dipped to fifty-eight percent in twenty twenty-six.

scene.title: % of US adults who own stock

lines.text: The workaround: fractional shares. You buy a slice of a share with dollars.
lines.say: The workaround is fractional shares, where you buy a slice of one share with dollars.

lines.text: Fidelity's minimum is $1. At Schwab, it's $5 for any S&P 500 stock.
lines.say: At Fidelity, a slice starts at one dollar, and at Schwab, five dollars for any S and P five hundred stock.

lines.text: $10 into a $250 share = 0.04 of a share, plus 4% of any dividend.
lines.say: So ten dollars into a two-hundred-fifty-dollar share buys four hundredths of it, plus four percent of any dividend it pays.

lines.text: Even the US Treasury sells I bonds from $25 and T-bills from $100.
lines.say: Even the US Treasury sells I bonds from twenty-five dollars and Treasury bills from one hundred.

lines.text: $5 a week adds up to $260 a year.
lines.say: And five dollars a week adds up to two hundred sixty dollars a year.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.ig:
4 in 10 Americans own zero stock. Yet $1 buys a slice.
Gallup, April 2026: 58% of US adults own stock, down from 62% in 2025, so 42% own none.
Fidelity's fractional shares start at $1; Schwab Stock Slices start at $5 per S&P 500 stock.
TreasuryDirect sells I bonds from $25 and T-bills from $100.
Sources: Gallup, Fidelity, Schwab, TreasuryDirect.
News and education, not financial advice.
